items.headline: China’s Aluminum Output Hits Record as Government Cap Looms
items.summary: Chinese aluminum production climbed to a record last month as smelters rushed to fill the global shortfall caused by the conflict in the Middle East.
items.author: Bloomberg News

items.headline: CATL Gets Approval for Battery Deal in Consolidation Push
items.summary: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. has been cleared to acquire a stake in a battery firm linked to one of China’s largest carmakers, highlighting Beijing’s growing support for consolidation in the sector.
items.author: Bloomberg News

items.headline: Petredec to Hire Gas Traders in Europe as It Expands Beyond LPG
items.summary: Petredec Ltd., the Singapore-based energy and shipping firm, plans to build a team of liquefied natural gas traders in Europe as it expands beyond its core liquefied petroleum gas business.
items.author: Eamon Akil Farhat

items.headline: Europe Builds SpaceX Rivals as Trump’s NASA Shifts Trans-Atlantic Space Ties
items.summary: For the second week in a row, Paris is presenting itself as the center of the space industry.
items.author: Kate Duffy

items.headline: EU Bank Breaks 40-Year Nuclear Taboo With Finnish Investment
items.summary: The European Investment Bank is investing €40 million ($46 million) in a Finnish small modular reactor start-up, breaking a four-decade nuclear hiatus as the continent races to develop new clean energy technologies.
items.author: John Ainger

items.headline: Volvo Pivots to Long-Range Hybrids as Full EVs Take More Time
items.summary: Volvo Car AB is rolling out new long-range plug-in hybrids in Europe and the US, betting demand for the dual technology will persist well into the next decade.
items.author: Rafaela Lindeberg

items.headline: Telefónica to Pay Streamer DAZN €1.65 Billion for LaLiga Matches
items.summary: Telefónica SA agreed to pay sports streamer DAZN Group Ltd. around €1.65 billion ($1.9 billion) for the rights to broadcast matches from Spain’s top football leagues over five seasons.
items.author: Clara Hernanz Lizarraga

items.headline: Cookie Maker’s Debt Falls Deeper Into Distress on Mounting Costs
items.summary: Biscuit International’s loans are sliding deeper into distress as declining sales volumes and cost pressures weigh on the business, just three months after a deal to extend and overhaul its debt.
items.author: Edward Clark

items.headline: TotalEnergies Partners With Mistral AI to Boost Oil Exploration
items.summary: TotalEnergies SE will work with French artificial intelligence startup Mistral AI to boost its oil and gas exploration abilities and extend the life of existing fields.
items.author: Francois de Beaupuy

items.headline: M&S Grocery Sales Soar as Hit From Cyberattack Fades, Data Show
items.summary: Marks & Spencer Group Plc’s grocery sales soared over the summer, according to retail tracker Worldpanel by Numerator, as the British supermarket bounced back after last year’s cyberattack.
items.author: Maddie Parker

items.headline: LVMH, Once Europe’s Largest Stock, Exits Top 10 by Value
items.summary: LVMH lost its crown as France’s most valuable company and dropped out of Europe’s top 10 listed firms, a symbolic reversal for the luxury giant that led the region’s market during the post-pandemic boom.
items.author: Julien Ponthus and Michael Msika

items.headline: Thailand Mulls 30% Tax on Imported EVs to Defend Industry, Finance Chief Says
items.summary: Thailand could impose an excise tax of around 30% on fully imported electric vehicles, Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas said, revealing for the first time the potential rate of a levy designed to steer automakers toward local production.
items.author: Haslinda Amin and Suttinee Yuvejwattana

items.headline: Italy Banks to Lend Ethiopia €400 Million for New Hydropower Dam
items.summary: Ethiopia is in negotiations with three Italian banks for €400 million in loans to complete the 1,800-megawatt Koysha dam.
items.author: Fasika Tadesse

items.headline: Kenya Joins African Nations Banning Unrefined-Mineral Exports
items.summary: Kenya will ban exports of unprocessed minerals and plans to build at least three refineries to purify gold, joining other African nations seeking to extract more value from the natural resources they produce.
items.author: Helen Nyambura

items.headline: Brazil’s Smaller Iron Ore Miners Battered by Shipping Costs
items.summary: Smaller Brazilian iron ore producers are struggling with soaring shipping costs to top consumer China, squeezing margins and prompting production cuts.
items.author: Mariana Durao and Katharine Gemmell

items.headline: Top Africa Clothes Retailer Pepkor Sinks on Earnings Outlook
items.summary: Pepkor Holdings Ltd. shares tumbled the most in more than three years after the South African discount clothing retailer forecast muted profit growth as the cost of building its new banking business weighs on profit.
items.author: Janice Kew

items.headline: JD Sports Names North America CEO, Chief Marketing Officer
items.summary: JD Sports Fashion Plc named new executives for marketing and North America as the sports retailer looks to reverse soft sales and an extended slump in the stock market.
items.author: Annie Bang

items.headline: GM to Offer Apple CarPlay After Shift Away From the System
items.summary: General Motors Co. is integrating Apple Inc.’s CarPlay in its latest infotainment system, three years after upsetting some consumers by eliminating the popular interface from its electric vehicles.
items.author: David Welch

items.headline: Vodacom to Appeal Kenya Court Ruling on Safaricom Stake Sale
items.summary: Vodacom Group Ltd. said it will appeal a Kenyan High Court decision invalidating the government’s sale of a stake in East Africa’s biggest mobile-network operator to the South African-based wireless carrier.
items.author: David Herbling

items.headline: Novonesis CEO Says EU Red Tape Risks Biosolutions Lead to China
items.summary: Europe risks surrendering its status as a global frontrunner in biosolutions to China unless it dramatically speeds up regulation and approvals, according to the woman who runs the world’s largest maker of industrial enzymes.
items.author: Sara Sjolin
